reason: Both conversations reached the correct 'stop using it, unplug it, get it checked' outcome once the hot-plastic smell was described, and neither identified the Beko fire-risk safety notice or the defrost timer. Conversation 1's opening was an unhelpful refusal that asked nothing, so the key smell description only came because the customer volunteered it; Conversation 2 instead distinguished musty-drain from burning-electrical smells, asked for the make/model (the right next question for an old Beko), and in its stop message added useful guidance to not open the back panel and to contact Beko directly. Conversation 2's speculative list of compressor/relay causes is unsupported and the replacement panel is a little commercial, but it still served the homeowner more completely and safely.
